presented_options.B: 0 = OK, 1 = any error (SQL, CLI, or IO collapsed together), with stderr distinguishing the category

presented_options.A: statements run without any transaction; durability is deferred to a periodic checkpoint
presented_options.B: statements run under a long-running implicit transaction that commits only when the process exits
presented_options.C: statements inherit the transaction of the previous BEGIN if any was ever opened in the session
presented_options.D: each statement is implicitly wrapped in its own transaction that commits on success, matching BEGIN/COMMIT semantics

answers.rationale: MiniDB-style durability normally gives autocommit semantics outside explicit transactions: each standalone statement is wrapped in an implicit transaction and committed on success.

presented_options.A: ARIES-style WAL with explicit undo and redo records plus a separate dirty-page table checkpoint
presented_options.B: shadow paging: mutations go to a copy page; a pointer swap at commit promotes the copy atomically
presented_options.C: synchronous double-write: every page is written to a scratch region before being written to its home location
presented_options.D: an append-only write-ahead log, replayed at startup to re-apply committed transactions and drop the uncommitted suffix

answers.rationale: The related recovery questions describe committed transactions being replayed and an uncommitted suffix being discarded, which matches an append-only WAL replay strategy rather than ARIES, shadow paging, or double-write pages.

presented_options.A: each record carries a CRC32; replay stops at the first record whose CRC fails to verify
presented_options.B: records are padded to a fixed 512-byte sector boundary; partial sectors are discarded
presented_options.C: records are written in pairs (main + mirror); replay prefers whichever pair verifies
presented_options.D: no per-record check; a single CRC covers the whole WAL file on clean shutdown

answers.rationale: The prompt's recovery behavior references CRC checks on WAL records. Per-record CRC32 with replay stopping at the first failed record is the standard simple protection against torn or partial WAL writes.

presented_options.A: a Volcano-style iterator tree: each operator exposes open/next/close and returns one row (or tiny batch) at a time
presented_options.B: push-based execution where operators drive their children forward via a single dataflow scheduler
presented_options.C: materialising execution: each operator fully computes its output set before the next operator starts reading
presented_options.D: vectorised/columnar execution where each operator produces and consumes batches of column vectors

answers.rationale: The physical-operator framing and references to open-time executor behavior point to a Volcano iterator model with open/next/close and incremental row production.

presented_options.A: an inverted list built lazily on first query and cached in memory
presented_options.B: a B-tree keyed by the composite (index_key, row_id); duplicates are naturally ordered by row_id
presented_options.C: a hash map keyed by the indexed value alone; collisions chain a Vec<RowId>
presented_options.D: a bitmap per distinct value; looked up with bitwise AND for compound predicates

answers.rationale: A durable secondary index in a small row-store is most plausibly represented as a B-tree over (index_key, row_id), which also handles duplicate indexed values by ordering on row_id.

presented_options.A: Filter and Project exist as separate types rather than being fused into one 'SelectExpr' operator
presented_options.B: IndexScan and SeqScan as two variants of a single ScanKind enum so the executor only has one Scan operator
presented_options.C: Update and Delete are distinct operators rather than one 'Mutate' operator parameterised by a kind
presented_options.D: SeqScan, IndexScan, Filter, Project, NestedLoopJoin, Sort, Limit, Insert, Update, Delete each as a distinct type

answers.rationale: The other options are mutually consistent with a codebase that exposes SeqScan, IndexScan, Filter, Project, NestedLoopJoin, Sort, Limit, Insert, Update, and Delete as distinct physical operators. A single Scan operator with a ScanKind enum conflicts with that shape.

presented_options.A: inside the storage layer, which transparently redirects SeqScan calls through the index when available
presented_options.B: inside the parser, encoded as a special AST node when the WHERE clause mentions an indexed column
presented_options.C: inside the planner when lowering the logical plan to a physical plan; the parser only produces ASTs
presented_options.D: inside the executor at open() time, after consulting the catalog to see whether an index is applicable

answers.rationale: Index selection belongs in planning, when lowering a logical plan into a physical plan. The parser should emit syntax only, and the executor should run the chosen physical operator.

presented_options.A: a single crate-wide error enum with one variant per source is the return type of top-level entry points; lower modules convert at their public boundary
presented_options.B: errors are propagated via panics with typed payloads and caught at the CLI via std::panic::catch_unwind

presented_options.D: each subsystem defines its own error type; the CLI sees a Box<dyn Error> and pattern-matches on downcast

answers.rationale: A crate-wide error enum with variants for IO, parse, type-check, and runtime errors is the cleanest fit for top-level entry points and for later CLI exit-code classification.

presented_options.A: the per-statement summary is written to stdout immediately before the data so callers see it arrive first
presented_options.B: per-statement summary lines (e.g. `ok 3 rows`) go to stderr, letting callers pipe stdout straight into another tool

presented_options.D: when --format json is active, the JSON value is the only thing on stdout — no banner lines, no trailing 'ok' line

answers.rationale: The stated contract separates data output from progress output. Writing summaries to stdout before data would pollute stdout and violate that contract; summaries should go to stderr or be suppressed by --quiet.

presented_options.A: the heap stores rows inside fixed-size pages rather than one file per row

presented_options.B: all three rows — every fsynced WAL record is replayed on startup

answers.rationale: The transaction has durable insert WAL records but no COMMIT record. Under the described WAL recovery model, only committed transactions are replayed, so the rows are not visible after recovery.
